top_story_title: SonicWall patches an exploited SonicOS SSL-VPN MFA bypass; CVE-2026-19868 is on CISA's KEV list with a 20 November due date
top_story_summary: SonicWall has released security updates for seven vulnerabilities in SonicOS firewalls. One of them, CVE-2026-19868, is already being exploited in attacks and was added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 6 November 2026 with a remediation due date of 20 November 2026. CISA describes it as a use of single-factor authentication weakness in SonicOS SSLVPN: a user who holds valid credentials for an alternate authentication method can bypass SAML authentication controls, and successful exploitation may also bypass SAML-enforced multi-factor authentication.
top_actions: Inventory SonicWall firewalls with SSL-VPN enabled and record the running SonicOS version per device; check the SonicWall PSIRT advisory for the fixed release for your platform and branch, and schedule the upgrade now rather than at the 20 November KEV due date.

Until the upgrade lands, restrict SSL-VPN reachability: limit the portal to known source countries/ASNs or a managed IP allowlist, and disable SSL-VPN entirely on appliances where remote access is not actually in use.

Remove every authentication path that is not SAML for SSL-VPN users - the flaw depends on the user holding valid credentials for an alternate method. Disable local-user SSL-VPN accounts and unused LDAP/RADIUS bindings on the SSL-VPN zone.
Terminate all active SSL-VPN sessions after upgrading and force re-authentication; assume session material may have been obtained.
Rotate local firewall admin credentials, API keys and VPN pre-shared keys after patching, and rotate passwords for any SSL-VPN account that could log in via a non-SAML method.
executive_summary: SonicWall: CVE-2026-19868, a SonicOS SSL-VPN single-factor authentication flaw that bypasses SAML-enforced MFA, is exploited in the wild and was KEV-listed on 6 November with a 20 November due date. It ships in a batch of seven SonicOS fixes. Patch, then rotate credentials and kill sessions.

Cisco published two advisories for upstream component flaws in Cisco products: the October 2026 Node.js set (four high-SIR CVEs, including KEV-listed Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497, KEV due 10 November) and the critical PHP "PHP2shell" pair CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both KEV-listed with a due date of 29 October that has already passed.

Cisco is also distrusting eight eMudhra intermediate CAs whose private keys can be brute-forced in seconds after a broken April 2025 key generation ceremony - a trust-store and certificate-validation problem on network gear, not a code vulnerability.
No fixed release numbers are stated in any source this cycle. Every upgrade below has to be matched to your platform and branch from the vendor advisory itself.

An OpenSSH flaw exploited within hours of disclosure (CVE-2026-123158) affects musl-based systems per the source; no network vendor has confirmed affected products, so it is tracked as a watch item rather than an appliance advisory.
Four of the ten collected items are not network infrastructure (WordPress, a SaaS breach by a runaway AI agent, an email-security integration blog, a general news roundup) and are dropped.
No vendor AI-defence capability is described in this cycle's sources, so nothing is recorded on the AI-defences page.
key_actions: **SonicWall** — Identify every SonicWall appliance with SSL-VPN enabled and record its running SonicOS version; match each against the fixed release in the SonicWall PSIRT advisory and upgrade, HA pair secondary first.

**SonicWall** — Before the upgrade window, remove non-SAML authentication paths from SSL-VPN: disable local SSL-VPN user accounts and any unused LDAP/RADIUS binding, since the flaw requires the user to hold credentials for an alternate method.
**SonicWall** — Read the SonicWall PSIRT advisory set directly to get all seven CVEs, their severities and the fixed build per platform - do not plan from the news summary.

**SonicWall** — Schedule a single upgrade to the fixed release across the SonicOS fleet instead of chasing the exploited CVE alone; upgrade the HA secondary first and verify config sync before failover.

**Cisco** — Open advisory cisco-sa-php-october26-Jj384Daq and extract the affected-product list; cross-reference it against your Cisco asset inventory by model and running version, and treat products absent from the list as not affected per Cisco.

**Cisco** — For every match, apply the fixed release named in the advisory, or the documented workaround if no maintenance window is available yet - the KEV due date of 29 October 2026 has already passed.

**Cisco** — Open advisory cisco-sa-oct2026-node-js-Jj3SQ19u, extract the affected-product list and match it against your Cisco inventory by model and running version; prioritise anything listed for CVE-2026-111497 against the 10 November 2026 KEV due date.
**Cisco** — Apply the fixed releases named in the advisory, scheduling core and management-platform devices into a change window and upgrading HA secondaries first.

headlines.title: SonicWall Patches Exploited SonicOS Vulnerability That Weakens VPN Logins
headlines.summary: An exploited SonicOS SSL-VPN authentication flaw lets anyone holding credentials for an alternate login method skip SAML-enforced MFA on SonicWall firewalls.

headlines.title: SonicWall warns of new SSL-VPN MFA bypass flaw exploited in attacks
headlines.summary: SonicWall shipped fixes for seven SonicOS firewall vulnerabilities, one of them an SSL-VPN authentication bypass already used in attacks.

headlines.title: Vulnerabilities in PHP Affecting Cisco Products: October 2026
headlines.summary: Two unauthenticated PHP RCE flaws dubbed PHP2shell, both KEV-listed with a due date that has already passed, affect Cisco products per Cisco's October 2026 advisory.

headlines.title: Vulnerabilities in Node.js and Brotli Affecting Cisco Products: October 2026
headlines.summary: Cisco's October 2026 Node.js advisory covers four high-severity flaws in Cisco products, including KEV-listed Brotli decoder write CVE-2026-111497, due 10 November.

headlines.title: Cisco Informational for Emergency Distrust of eMudhra Root and Intermediate Certificate Authorities
headlines.summary: Cisco is emergency-distrusting eight eMudhra intermediate CAs whose private keys can be brute-forced in seconds after a broken 2025 key generation ceremony.

headlines.title: OpenSSH flaw exploited in the wild just hours after disclosure (CVE-2026-123158)
headlines.summary: OpenSSH CVE-2026-123158 lets anyone reaching the SSH port log into passwordless accounts on musl-based systems, exploited within hours of the 5 November fix.
